i declare resumed the session adjourned on thursday 18 december 2008. i would like to wish you all, ladies and gentlemen, a happy new year - a happy 2009 which will hopefully bring us further on the road to european unity. may we succeed in promoting peace in the world. i can now make a statement on this.
i am not going to go into detail. the conference of presidents has asked me to make a statement on the events in the middle east. the debate will take place on wednesday afternoon, in the presence of the president of the foreign ministers' council, mr schwarzenberg, the czech foreign minister. i'm bringing this up because it wasn't clear. we have made a great effort and have found a great warmly for this. i am not going to go into detail. as we gather here for a plenary session at the beginning of this new year, people are dying again in the middle east. i cannot help but feel - and i think most of us do - that when i look at the television images, a bitter memory of "déjà vu" comes to mind. on behalf of the european parliament, i would like to express my deep regret at the escalation of the conflict between israel and hamas in gaza. i want to make it very clear that it is not acceptable that the suffering of the population continues in such a way that violence continues and that now united nations personnel are being targeted. how far must the spiral of violence continue before insight and reason prevail? there must be an immediate end to the violence on both sides. it is totally unacceptable and must be strongly criticised that hamas is firing rockets at israeli cities. and we must not forget that it was hamas that ended the ceasefire. but the response must not ignore the proportionality of the means. all people in the middle east have equal dignity. the inalienable right of a state to protect itself does not justify acts of violence which primarily affect the civilian population. the people of gaza need help urgently. the dignity of a palestinian is the same as that of an israeli or a european or an american - all people on this earth are equal. we must not allow the humanitarian situation to deteriorate. we must be prepared, as political leaders, to make a determined contribution to finding a lasting solution to the spiral of violence, beyond the short-term situation. the reduction of security to purely military aspects is, in my view, doomed to failure. there can therefore be no purely military solution to the middle east problem. we must finally reach a political solution. this means, first and foremost, learning from the failure of the previous approach. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. i have been in contact over the last few days by telephone with the israeli president, mr peres, with the prime minister of the palestinian authority, mr salam fayad, with the president of the knesset, mrs dalia itzik, and of course with the high representative of the european union for foreign affairs and security policy, mr javier solana, who has been in the region for a very long time. i have also been in contact with the vice-presidents of the euro-mediterranean parliamentary assembly, because i am currently chairing the euro-mediterranean assembly, namely the president of the jordanian parliament, abdel hadi al-majali, the president of the italian chamber of deputies, gianfranco fini, and the president of the moroccan parliament, mustapha mansouri. in all these discussions i have always made it clear that the european parliament fully supports the demands which the council of ministers has made for the european union and which were confirmed by the united nations security council resolution of 8 january. it is sad that this legally binding security council resolution, which the americans abstained from, thus making the resolution possible, is being ignored by both sides in the conflict, israel and hamas. there must be an immediate and permanent ceasefire. this ceasefire must be achieved with the mediation of egypt and the involvement of all actors. immediate unhindered access for humanitarian aid must be ensured and the united nations work and relief agency (unrwa) must be enabled to continue its humanitarian activities without hindrance. and i would add, not just for three hours a day! if the humanitarian organizations and the united nations have to stop their work because the belligerents do not respect their neutrality, we have reached a low point in international law and humanity that we cannot accept. the third requirement is the intensification of the peace process. the only viable basis for lasting peace is and remains a two-state solution with israel and palestine as sovereign states within secure borders. the european union, together with the members of the quartet, the moderate arab partners and all parties to the conflict under the auspices of the united nations, must bring about a rapid resumption of peace negotiations. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we must now ask ourselves what method we have used to date in the so-called peace process. despite the known difficult environment and the scarcely tangible progress, it was possible to assume until a few weeks ago that we were in a negotiating logic. the international community, and above all the european union, has supported these negotiations with a strong commitment and has helped financially to create the conditions for the establishment of a palestinian state. but was this commitment politically strong enough? that is a question we must ask ourselves. we are now back to the logic of escalation. understandably, in times of crisis management, people tend to think short-term. we need an immediate ceasefire and a complete withdrawal of israeli forces, as called for by the un security council. the experience of the past decades has taught us that peace in the middle east cannot come from the region alone. but it will not be possible without reconciliation between the warring parties. the international community must therefore be prepared to promote peace in the middle east more than ever before, so that the bitter events of the past few decades do not remain bitter experiences for decades to come. international troops can and must help to secure a ceasefire. we must therefore make every effort to ensure that the egyptian-french plan to set up an international mechanism to secure the borders of gaza is a real success, and of course the smuggling of arms and rockets into the gaza area must be stopped as a matter of priority. the european union had already indicated its readiness to engage in this way in its action strategy paper at the beginning of the annapolis process. but let me emphasize one thing in particular: the deployment of european and international security forces must not guarantee the silencing of arms in the short term. it must have a clear political objective, namely to build the confidence needed to conclude the peace talks by guaranteeing security for israelis and palestinians alike. this means that with a possible use of troops, which only makes sense with a robust mandate, the political influence on all sides is increased to reach a peaceful solution. we need more than the repeated commitment to peace, which we have so often expressed as a goal in the past. what we need is the willingness not just to seek peace but to make it happen before the decades of hatred escalate further and cause a conflagration. in conclusion, i would like to recall that 2008 was the european year of intercultural dialogue. i would remind you of how much we, as the european parliament, have worked to make this year a year of hope and to put political emphasis on the fact that the clash of cultures is not a law of nature. the global reaction to the war in gaza shows how quickly efforts at intercultural dialogue can be derailed when overtaken by the reality of the images we see in the news every day. worse still, this reality plays into the hands of extremists and fundamentalists whose aim is not peace but to drive the spiral of confrontation. violence creates violence. this insight cannot be repeated often enough. only dialogue and negotiation can provide a way out of the crisis. both are not ends in themselves, but must be courageously pursued with the aim that the people of israel and palestine can live in real security, in peace and with respect for their dignity. the rapporteur. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. we have today the result of many discussions and negotiations, some of which were very emotional, and we shall be able to vote on it tomorrow. we didn't make it easy. the negotiations with the council and the commission were a struggle to find the right solutions. we have found that science does not always provide clear evidence to show the only right way. further scientific monitoring will be necessary to evaluate the impact of this new legislation. first of all, therefore, i would like to thank all those who contributed to this good result with their constructive proposals, my colleagues in this parliament, the european commission, the french presidency of the council - sorry that the czech presidency of the council is not here tonight - but also thank the staff. the directive on the sustainable use of plant protection products, which is now in force, is a major step towards greater common ground in european environmental and consumer protection. sustainability as the guiding principle of our european agriculture guarantees healthy food and a healthy environment. for the first time, the handling of plant protection products is harmonised at european level. the principle of "as much as necessary, as little as possible" requires a comprehensive, sound knowledge. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. they must be used in the right way to work properly: at the right time, in the right medication, in the right dose. this includes considering whether chemical plant protection is necessary or whether mechanical measures are more appropriate. the choice of the best technology and proven planting equipment protects the environment and the user and contributes to the success of the farm by producing good harvests. member states shall set out in their national action plans measures to reduce the use of plant protection products. the reduction of risk is the ultimate objective. the application of the general principles of integrated pest management will be made mandatory throughout the european union from 2014. the implementation of the water framework directive is a top priority. member states shall establish buffer zones for bodies of water which must be adapted to the soil and geographical conditions. the use of plant protection products in the municipal area and in protected areas shall be minimised or, where appropriate, eliminated. there are rules for the inspection of equipment and regular maintenance intervals are established. risk reduction includes the provision of sound training and education to professional users in the field of pesticide use. when selling plant protection products, private users who are not specifically trained and who may cause damage by improper use in private gardens must be instructed and informed by a well-trained seller about the use and the risks. the directive brings together the different rules that have been in place in the member states at a high level. the measures envisaged are in the interests of the environment, consumers and users. the same conditions throughout the european union guarantee the same safety standards and production conditions. we agree that substances which have been shown to be harmful to health should not be authorized. but a ban must be based on scientific knowledge and not on political dogma. and you have to look at exposure, because with pesticides, like with a lot of things in life, the dose makes the poison. one headache pill is a blessing, but if we take 20, it's dangerous, life-threatening. we have reached a good compromise. it reconciles environmental and economic policy, and i hope that tomorrow we will be able to make our demands clearer in a clear vote. i would like to make a technical point: there is an error in article 14 (4). reference is made to the internet portal member of the commission. - the madam president, i would like to thank all those who have spoken in today's debate for their very constructive contributions. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used to the full, and that the member states are able to take part in the implementation of the community's financial instruments. is a major step forward which, in addition to protecting the health of european citizens and the environment, will bring economic benefits due to reduced costs to national health systems, and another benefit will be the reduced use of pesticides resulting from this legislation. in addition to the national action plans, the proposed compromise package contains a number of other important aspects. the precautionary principle must be respected. in the context of integrated pest management, other non-chemical plant protection methods shall be given priority. the protection of areas and persons passing through is strengthened. in particular, national action plans may include provisions on the information of persons who may be exposed to moving spray clouds, and areas to be sprayed by air should not be adjacent to populated areas. all distributors of pesticides, not just those selling to professional users, will ensure that some of their staff have a specific certificate of competence, which will of course be mutually recognisable, to provide information on pesticides and to be available to customers for advice. only certain categories of small distributors will be exempted from this obligation. as regards the air spray ban, a compromise solution was found to deal with the requests for exemption. the exemption will follow a two-step procedure. first, the preparation of a general aerial spraying plan, which will be subject to explicit approval by the authorities, and then the submission of specific aerial spraying applications, where appropriate, which will be subject to the conditions for approval of the general plan. in conclusion, i would like to add that the commission is satisfied with the outcome of the negotiations and is therefore able to accept the proposed compromise amendments in full.
member of the commission. − madam president, thank you all for your very fruitful participation in this very interesting debate. the commission has attached particular importance to this file and i have been personally committed to the highest level of public health which it seeks to achieve. there have been long and difficult discussions during the trialogue which the rapporteur has steered with great dedication and skill, and i thank her for that. the commission supported the common position and can now support the proposal as it emerges from the second reading. all the innovative aspects of the proposal have been retained, in particular the approval criteria, which will ensure that dangerous substances which pose a high risk to public health are eliminated or substituted by safer alternatives, improved mutual recognition, and the substitution of some products by safer alternatives. let me reply, however, to some of the comments that have been made here. according to the commission’s estimate, only 4% of the substances currently on the market would disappear because they are endocrine disruptors and only 2% because they are carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic to production. the total number of active substances which are currently on the market and which possibly would not be approved under the new regulation is expected to be less than 25 substances. this evaluation has been confirmed by a report from the swedish chemical agency and is also in line with the revised impact assessment from the uk pesticides safety directorate. moreover, i would like to point out that the new criteria will apply to substances already approved only upon renewal of their approval, and for most of them the renewal date is 2016. the industry will therefore have ample time to develop other safer substances. i would also like to make reference to some comments made about imported food. let me remind you that, as from 2008, we have the regulation on maximum residue levels which is fully applicable. if an active substance is not approved for use in plant reduction products in the eu, the maximum residue level for this substance is set at the level of detection. this mrl is valid for eu production, but also for imported food and feed. there are, however, several reasons why an active substance could not be approved in the eu, and the possible risk to consumers is only one of them. others can be linked to environmental issues or the protection of workers, which fall under the sovereignty of third countries where the pesticide is used. in these circumstances the use of the pesticide could not be acceptable for us, but the treated crops would not necessarily pose a risk to eu consumers. the third country which wants to export commodities treated with such substances to the eu may therefore ask for an import tolerance as long as it can submit data proving that there is no risk to human health from the consumption of these commodities and that these data are favourably evaluated by efsa and formally adopted in eu legislation. this is the position regarding imported goods. coming back to the directive which we are hopefully about to adopt, the commission considers the final compromise to be properly balanced, to achieve the objectives of health and environmental production, as well as to ensure the availability of pesticides to farmers. we now look forward to the formalisation of the second-reading agreement. this is certainly a very good way for the european parliament and the council to start a new year, and good for our citizens as it benefits their health. it is also, we believe, beneficial to our farmers as it ensures their own production through specific measures, such as the promotion of safer products. what was achieved is important. it was achieved by all of us together and serves as an excellent example of how interinstitutional cooperation can directly benefit our citizens.

reform was clearly to ensure that the competitiveness of the european fund industry is increased, that the fund industry is enabled to reduce its costs, to develop and exploit economies of scale, to a management company passport; secondly, the facilitation of cross-border fund mergers to ensure that the number of funds offered in the european union is reduced and thus the imbalance we see between europe and, above all, the usa can be overcome; thirdly, the possibility of so-called master-feeder structures, i.e. the possibility for one fund to invest in another master fund and have the investments managed through that master fund; fourthly, the development of a short, i.e. only two-page information document containing the most important information for the small investor, the president of the eurogroup. - mr president of the european parliament, mr president of the republic, mr president, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, over the last fifty years europe has often demonstrated its ability to formulate great ambitions and also to develop the spirit and determination necessary to implement, in a consistent manner, the ambitions it cherishes. the european union itself is the best example of this, as is the internal market, as is enlargement, that is to say, the reunion between european geography and european history, as is the economic and monetary union, whose tenth anniversary we are celebrating today. the road to economic and monetary union and the introduction of our single currency was a long one, and the genesis of economic and monetary union, with the initial impetus given by the werner report as early as 1970, proves this. the long genesis of the monetary snake, the european monetary system, the creation of the ecu in 1979, the delors plan of 1989, the maastricht treaty of 1992, as well as the danish no and the french yes, which were called small at the time, not to mention the crisis of the european monetary system in 1993. this whole journey has not been without difficulties and bumps. many at the time were the critics of the single currency, both in political and academic circles, not to mention an impressive number of central bankers, who believed that economic and monetary union could not or should not be achieved and that, if it were to be achieved anyway, the single currency would, in the end, be weak and without any future. it is important to me to take the opportunity of the tenth anniversary of this landmark event in european integration to pay tribute, in my turn, to those men who created the euro, such as pierre werner, helmut kohl, françois mitterrand, jacques delors, valéry giscard d'estaing and others. i would like to congratulate them once again on their vision, their determination and their unwavering commitment to europe. the men i mentioned and many others who followed them could not have imagined the rapid success of their political project. since 1 january this year, 16 member states have been participating in economic and monetary union and the euro is the currency of almost 330 million european citizens. the euro has thus become the most tangible sign of european integration. the euro is a tangible sign of stability, recognised throughout the world. it protects its citizens from the worst consequences of the economic crisis. after ten years, it is clear that the euro is an undeniable success. but anniversaries are only worth celebrating if they are bridges to the future, because it is also clear that, despite the collective indulgence in self-congratulation, the real tests for the cohesion and coherence of the euro area are still ahead of us. 2009 will be an extremely difficult year for the euro area economies and for european citizens, and there will be many challenges to be faced, both internally and externally. internally, euro area governments will need to act together to contain the effects of the economic crisis and to invest in the structural foundations of the economy to build a bridge to the post-crisis period. exceptional situations call for exceptional measures. we must not lose sight of the fact that the protective screen that the euro has erected around our economies did not fall from the sky. euro area economies are better protected against adverse economic developments because membership of the euro area is a mark of quality certifying to its members a real capacity to implement prudent macroeconomic policies and policies geared towards sustainable growth and prosperity for its citizens. the protection afforded by the euro is therefore directly linked to our credibility, which is based on the ability to implement these policies there. this credibility is the foundation of the benefits of economic and monetary union and we will need to preserve it if we are to continue to enjoy the full benefits of the single currency. on the external front, we will have to draw political lessons from the international financial and economic crisis. there is a direct causal link between the current crisis, which originated in the united states, and the persistence of major global imbalances. the lack of adequate transparency, accountability and integrity in the financial sector was then a catalyst for the crisis. the restoration of stability to the global financial and real economy implies a thorough reform of the financial system, but also the elimination of the important imbalances in the mix between aggregate consumption and aggregate saving. this rebalancing requires the active collaboration of the major economies in america, asia and europe. however, despite significant progress, the international representation of the euro is still often too fragmented and national interests too often trump the common interest, preventing the euro area from fully assuming the political responsibility corresponding to its economic weight and from realising all the economic benefits of economic and monetary union. economic and monetary union is an economic project, but it is first and foremost a political project. we must therefore use the second decade of the euro to complete economic and monetary union by strengthening its political bodies at both internal and external levels.

after a period of semi-dormancy between 1980 and 1988, progress was resumed when the council set up the committee chaired by jacques delors, which led to the signing of the maastricht treaty. we the bank of france, who was then bernard clappier, co-author of the robert schuman declaration in 1950; mr lamfalussy, who brought his great expertise, almost unique, to the work of the committee on european monetary union which we had set up with helmut schmidt to relaunch the project; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. to all of them, today, we must say a big thank you. what can we say about the euro on this tenth anniversary, which is being celebrated in a time of crisis? what are our birthday toasts? firstly, the success of the euro has exceeded the expectations not only of all its opponents, of course, but also of all its promoters. i don't want to go into details, but you gave me five minutes. in my conversations with the leading monetary experts in the years 1995-2000, they were all sceptical about the possibility of introducing and succeeding with the euro. in 10 years the euro has become the second most important currency in the world and, as mentioned earlier, one of the most respected. its good management has made it a shield against the crisis and a foundation for growth without inflation. without the euro, continental europe would be shaken by a monetary storm that would worsen the economic crisis. we expect monetary policy to try to contain, within the limits of the power of money, the depressing effect of the crisis and to prepare for the return, which is not yet being addressed, to growth without inflation when the heavy public deficits and debt generated by the crisis have to be balanced. we have confidence in the leadership and staff of the european central bank, who have shown their expertise since the beginning of the crisis and whose determination and independence we respect. two final remarks. but let us beware of giving the euro a global dimension which would flatter our vanity but increase our risks. the euro is the currency of the european continent and must express its particular culture of reason and stability in concert with the other world currencies. finally, i do not think that public opinion should be kept waiting too long for the banking regulation of the euro area to be put in order. it seems to me that the european central bank could be called upon, in accordance with article 106 (5) of the maastricht treaty, to conduct this adjustment and to supervise its application. what is needed is a strong impetus, expertise and a timetable for decisions which the central bank could draw up and which the council of ministers of the euro area, chaired by you, mr president juncker, could then adopt and implement. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that the symbol of integration which the success of the euro is must give us the courage to go further in building the ever more united europe which the treaties propose and which we are struggling to put into place. the inevitability of failure is contrasted with the dynamics of success. success today has a beautiful name, it is called the euro. members of the economic and monetary affairs advisory committee. - mr president, i have to say something. ten years of the euro is indeed a cause for celebration. if anyone had said ten years ago that the euro was developing as splendidly as it has, they would have been ridiculed. many people worked on this success, and i remember many skeptical voices -- premature birth and not viable project was talked about -- and today we know that it was a vision that many people worked on. the speakers who have spoken have reminded us of all those who contributed to the milestones, the european monetary system, which was an agreement between central banks to set central rates, the delors report which envisaged the introduction of monetary union in three stages, the maastricht treaty - just two years after the fall of the wall - the transitional periods - and many contributed to the fact that the euro has become such a successful project today. parliament - mrs berès has already said this as chairman of the committee - has actively participated in many reports, discussions, opinions and proposals during this period, particularly from 1994, when the maastricht treaty was implemented, until 2002, when cash was introduced, and i would like to thank in particular the two committee chairmen during this period, karl von wogau and christa randzio-plath, who also represented parliament externally and provided the necessary parliamentary support for this project, which was originally created by the governments. we are still trying to achieve the same representation today under the presidency of mrs berès. the report by mrs berès, which we adopted by a large majority on 18 november, describes the successes, the challenges, the risks and the problems, and i would like to add a few points to what mrs berès has said. the euro is a great success and a unique project: a central monetary policy under the guidance of the european central bank and a decentralised budgetary and financial policy. it is important that the link between these two levels of responsibility in the stability and growth pact be maintained in future, also in times of crisis. without this stability and growth pact, without greater coordination of budgetary and financial policies, the euro will continue to face risks that we can avoid. i would like to ask the member states of the euro zone in particular, but also the european union as a whole, to take this discipline, this coordinated cooperation, more seriously than they have in the past on one or another issue. the euro has brought down inflation considerably. it has created confidence and stability and has become the second reserve currency in a period when no one else had the confidence to do so. the euro has increased the pressure for structural reform in the member states and has thus become a fitness programme for companies and for states in times of globalisation. the institutions of the eurozone - as several of my predecessors have pointed out - the ecofin council, the euro group, many other institutions, together with the commission and the european central bank, created the necessary conditions because they were already functioning, because they were there, because they acted independently to respond quickly, reliably and correctly to the economic crisis. we have seen the euro as the lever for creating a european financial market. the political conclusion of these joint achievements is that countries with a common currency and a common internal market have reached a unique stage of integration that ensures peace and prosperity. but the euro is not necessarily a self-sufficient future. there are a number of specific suggestions and demands that risks should be taken seriously: the drifting of economies, which poses a considerable risk to wage developments and budget deficits, should not be ignored on the occasion of an anniversary. a completely different aspect is the different development of interest rates on government bonds. we are now seeing the interest rate differential, which has certainly narrowed, widening again, so that new problems may arise for individual euro-zone member states. i would like to remind you that there should be no special discount, particularly when the eurozone is enlarged, and that all the countries that join the eurozone must and can fulfil these conditions of the maastricht treaty. the euro has reached the citizens. he's earned the trust of the world. it has passed the first test and is a unique contribution to the lasting integration of our peoples in europe. we can all be proud of that. thank you, sir. the commission is therefore proposing to amend the proposal. the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. i am very sorry that relatively few colleagues are attending this ceremony today, because it is indeed something of an historic event. we have already heard from the various speakers how great was the scepticism at the beginning of the introduction of the euro. the belief that we could not manage the logistical tasks of introducing billions of banknotes and coins on our own, and that it was indeed possible to combine a common monetary policy with a fiscal policy that was still separate in the individual member states, was not only seen as a great challenge but as simply unrealizable. well, the facts speak a different language. the european monetary union is a fact. the euro has been in existence for ten years. we have what seems to be a small political miracle, and once again the words of walter hallstein, the first president of the commission, are being fulfilled: 'in european affairs, those who do not believe in miracles are not realists.' the doubts of the citizens, which certainly existed in many member states at the beginning, who believed that the euro was an enormous cost, have now disappeared. today the euro is accepted, even enthusiastically by many citizens. it has become something of a visible european identification tool. it is one of the few symbols we have today, along with the anthem and the flag. it can be said that in the first years of the european central bank's existence europe and the european economy were sailing in relatively calm waters and that therefore it was not so difficult for the european central bank to pursue a policy of stability. but at least we have to note that the average inflation rate in the first ten years of the euro is around 2%, practically on the target set by the european central bank, whereas in the fifty years of the existence of the d-mark, which has always been a model of stability, we had an average inflation of 3%, so we can speak of a good performance by the european central bank. but their true strength, their true quality, they show now, in a moment of crisis. it plays a very important role here. it is independent, efficient, self-confident, and it acts decisively and quickly. it has become a model for some central banks in europe in countries not yet in the euro area, but also outside europe. it shows the fed in the united states very clearly that it can make a successful policy, not because it is independent, but precisely because it is politically independent and not bound by the instructions of the various governments. we know that at the moment, after the banking sector has been bailed out in the individual member states, the member states are developing various economic recovery programmes to cushion the negative effects of the financial crisis on the real economy. this will present new challenges for the european central bank, because there is a risk that the different approaches will lead to distortions of competition and that the convergence we have already achieved between some of the members of the euro area will be lost and we will have increasingly divergent developments. this is where the countersteering comes in. that is why it is so crucial and important that the stability and growth pact is not abandoned, but that we ensure that it remains in force. this is why it is so important that the necessary structural reforms, which the commission and the ecb have repeatedly called for in the past, are indeed pursued in the individual member states. the european central bank will have a new task in the next few years. the crisis has taught us that we need something like a european financial market supervision. the european central bank can play a major role in this. it has in principle indicated its willingness to introduce something like a central european supervisory system, analogous to the european system of central banks. the international role of the euro must be further strengthened. the eurozone should be able to speak with one voice and to have a central, unified voice in international organisations such as the imf and the oecd. one thing remains: a common currency without a common fiscal policy is and will remain a risky undertaking. this is not a petition. the eu also faces major challenges. we have high unemployment, which is unfortunately on the rise again, we have demographic change, we have pressure to migrate, we have increasing poverty among certain groups and increased competition as a result of globalisation. the eurozone can only meet these challenges if the economic policies of the member states are more closely interlinked. the appointment of a president of the eurozone was a first step in that direction, but only a first step. more must follow.
president of latvia. - mr president, distinguished members, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the president of the european parliament for his kind words of introduction and for the invitation to address the elected representatives of the european nations. i'm honored to have this opportunity. it is a great pleasure for me to address the european parliament in my native latvian, especially since latvian has also been the official language of communication of the european union for the past five years. i am speaking to you today as the first term of office of the latvian elected representatives in the european parliament draws to a close. thank you for the honor of doing your duty. dear members, 2009 is a very important year for latvia today marks the fifth anniversary of latvia's accession to the european union and nato. after the restoration of latvia's independence in 1991, participation in these international organisations became a strategic objective for latvia. latvia has made clear its willingness to participate in european and transatlantic economic and security structures. the expansion of the european family of democracies in the first decade of the 21st century marked the most dynamic change in europe since the creation of the european union. this was a major change. the european institutions have been joined by countries that have long been violently isolated from them, despite the fact that these countries historically shared the values that have formed the basis of the european union. last november 18, latvia celebrated the 90th anniversary of its proclamation as a country. this anniversary is very important for our nation, it once again confirmed our unwavering desire to live in an independent, free and democratic country. the act of proclamation of the republic of latvia in 1918 proclaimed: "[...] all citizens, regardless of their nationality, are invited to help, because latvia will guarantee the rights of all people, it will be a democratic and just state, in which there will be no place for oppression and injustice. i'm very proud of that. thirty years before the adoption of the universal declaration of human rights, the republic of latvia showed its commitment to its fundamental values and principles. latvia has always felt a sense of belonging to europe and its values, even when latvia and other central and eastern european countries were long associated with a country where many values were viewed through a particular ideological prism. there was peace between the eastern bloc countries, but it was a prison-yard peace. this was achieved by the presence of tanks, repression and threats. the inhumanity of totalitarian ideology was brought to your attention, members of parliament, and to the attention of europe as a whole last year by the film 'the story of the podomyu' by the latvian director edwin šnoras. we have shared a history, but we have shared different destinies. you need to look to the past to understand each other better and to look together to the future, and i would like to thank the european parliament for the declaration it adopted on 22 september last year on the proclamation of 23 august as european day of remembrance for the victims of stalinism and nazism. this declaration reminds all european citizens of the tragic events in the history of latvia and all of europe. today i want to look at a lot of recent history. this year marks the fifth anniversary of latvia's membership of the european union and nato. what has this period been like for latvia? what are the benefits to our country? what has our country achieved and what challenges lie ahead? first, the post-participation process in europe has helped to consolidate democracy in our society and has facilitated the development of democratic institutions. by joining the european union, latvia has demonstrated its commitment to its future, a future based on the european identity and our common values of freedom and democracy, responsibility, rule of law and human rights, equality and tolerance, prosperity. secondly, the accession to the european union has significantly improved the investment climate in latvia. the 'european currency', as the european union's structural funds are known in the vernacular, has made a significant contribution to the development of latvia's economy. third, we can enjoy the benefits of free movement. it is so common and natural to travel freely within the schengen area, and it is so natural to study, work and gain experience in other eu member states. fourth, the free movement of goods and services has opened up new business opportunities. every entrepreneur and consumer can operate in a free environment without borders and customs duties. this is particularly important for us in a country with a small internal market. fifth, and this is the most important, latvia's voice is heard in europe and europe's voice is heard in the world. we can be proud to have such a unique mechanism of cooperation at our disposal. it allows us all to work together actively to find solutions to global challenges, climate and demographic change, energy security, migration and financial crises, all on a global scale. latvia now has new political and economic instruments at its disposal, but it should be noted that the state's responsibility for the future of europe as a whole has also increased significantly, it is a responsibility towards all european citizens. looking back on successes should also be critical and acknowledging mistakes made. after joining the european union, the latvian government had a sense of accomplishment, the goal had been achieved. we didn't realize that we were at the beginning of the process, not the end. the european union offers a wealth of opportunities, but each country and each society must seize them. we have not used all the possibilities in latvia, we have not always implemented cohesion policy wisely and we have not always used the financial possibilities provided. our national institutions have had to learn to live in the european union. we have not been sufficiently determined to introduce the euro, which is one of the biggest mistakes we have made in the process of euro integration, and this is particularly evident in the current financial crisis. but even the most ardent eurosceptic must admit that latvia's membership of the european union has a positive balance. would anyone in latvia want to return to europe, where there are customs barriers between countries? no, you won't! would anyone want to stand in line at the border to enter a neighboring country? no, you won't! does anyone want to go back to restrictions on labour mobility, education and experience? no, you won't! even skeptics quickly become accustomed to good things, becoming simply skeptical. ladies and gentlemen, the deterioration of the financial system and the economy in recent months has irrevocably changed the role and role of national governments in economic processes. until now, financial markets have been able to develop very freely. we were convinced that market laws would be a sufficiently effective driver of economic development. we believed that the market would keep things in place. it happens. markets regulate themselves. but in the context of this global crisis, we see that our financial systems and our economies are suffering, and, most importantly, that our citizens, the people, are suffering. events at the end of last year have demonstrated the need for more active involvement of national governments in economic processes. the current approach of steering economically has been irresponsible. unfortunately, we woke up too late. i wish i could see the obstacle ahead of me - the financial meltdown - but i can't avoid it. this situation requires a comprehensive approach at national, european and global levels. coordinated action at the global level is needed to restore economic growth. this will only be possible by creating a new architecture and mechanisms for the financial system. a strict system of supervision will be required, while not restricting initiative and market processes. finding that balance will be the most difficult challenge. at european level, we have a significant advantage in coordinating our activities, in taking common action and in finding a sustainable solution. we are pleased with the progress made by the european commission in developing an action plan for economic recovery. it's a vital step out of the mess we're in right now. i'm going to be delaying national solutions for a while. the global financial crisis has also affected latvia. the commission has also received comments from the latvian authorities, which have submitted comments on the restructuring plan. the latvian authorities have also provided information on the implementation of the restructuring plan. it is a difficult task, but we can only overcome the crisis if we see a safe way out of it, without confusing short-term solutions with a long-term vision of economic development. at the end of last year, six positions and opposition parties represented in the latvian parliament agreed on a common position to support the economic stabilisation plan developed by the latvian government. this agreement provides for special attention to be paid to the monitoring of the use of the loan granted to latvia. the plan sets out the medium-term priorities of the latvian economy: export support, promotion of free and fair competition, substantial reduction of the current account deficit in the balance of payments and introduction of the euro in 2012. latvia's accession to the euro area has become one of the country's most important strategic objectives. it is essential that latvia is not left alone in this situation. it is not just international financial organisations that are helping us to get through these difficult times, but also the institutions of the european union and the european countries. latvia is grateful for this expression of solidarity. ladies and gentlemen! each enlargement has not only added new countries to the european union, but also placed new emphases on its agenda, including foreign policy. latvia's accession to the european union took place at a time when the european neighbourhood policy, its objectives, principles and implementing instruments were being defined. since then, the european union's external action towards its eastern neighbours has increased in particular. this has been achieved thanks to the interest and experience of the new member states. latvia has always seen the wider dimension of neighbourhood policy. latvia will continue to play an active role in the definition and implementation of this policy. this policy is not limited to the european union's relations with certain countries those with which it shares a land or sea border. in the context of this policy, the place and role of the european union in the world must be discussed. latvia, together with a number of like-minded countries, has actively promoted closer european union involvement in the eastern neighbourhood region. a new policy initiative, the 'eastern partnership', has emerged to transform the common european neighbourhood policy and adapt it to the specificities of the region, making the process more active, bold and ambitious. latvia welcomes the proposals prepared by the european commission. the eastern partnership in practice must strengthen political and economic relations between the european union and the countries of the region, as well as strengthen cooperation between the countries of the region. the eastern partnership should be developed with a view to respecting the principle of differentiation, individual assessment and treatment of each partner. each of these countries has its own development path. there are countries that want to see themselves in the european union, and there are countries that have other goals. our policy will only succeed if we are able to work with all the countries in the region, understandingly helping where needed. positive signals for broadening and deepening cooperation were also received during my visits to the countries of central asia last october, when i visited kazakhstan, uzbekistan and turkmenistan. latvia is and will remain an active supporter and implementer of the european neighbourhood policy. each european country has its own historical experience and its own opportunities to work on our common project for the benefit of the european union. latvia's special contribution to the eastern dimension is the mutual trust and expertise that our bilateral relations have built up over a period of common history. latvia is obliged to take advantage of this special situation. in the next decade, it may be lost. in a few decades, latvia will be seen in the east as just one of the countries of the european union, not the gateway to europe. latvia has a strong political commitment to the eu and its member states, and has a strong commitment to the eu's external relations. it's a win-win. we also get to hear the neighbours' views on the future relationship with the european union. i am convinced that it is in europe's interest to inaugurate the eastern partnership during the czech presidency. ladies and gentlemen, in the first days of the czech presidency, the question of energy security has become a new topic. the financial and economic crisis has a cyclical nature. energy security and sustainable energy sources are on the european and global political agenda at all times. it's becoming more and more relevant. energy security has a strong external dimension. this means that we cannot look at this question in isolation from the situation in the world. this is also borne out by recent events in ukraine and the conflict in georgia. in the recent past, the member states of the european union have considered energy as a national issue rather than an eu issue. the energy developments of recent years, the interruption of energy supplies, the decline in energy resources and the fluctuation of prices have contributed to a common understanding among the member states of the european union of the need for a common energy policy. at the intersection of energy and policy, the key is to ensure a regular, sufficient, economic and sustainable supply of environmentally friendly energy. it is recognised that the european union's contribution in this area has been mixed. in some areas, such as the development of an environmentally friendly energy economy, we have set ambitious targets at european level that need to be met. in other areas, we are only at the beginning of the diversification of energy sources and the integration of energy markets at european level. recent events the russian gas supply disruption have highlighted the need for a swifter solution at pan-european level. it is our collective responsibility to use this shared understanding to create a truly integrated and diversified european energy market. we must not let our resolve fade with this spring snow. energy security can only be successfully addressed through active dialogue with transit and supply countries. the european union has the foreign policy instruments to deal with this issue. it is our responsibility to use them. another area where serious work is needed is the integration of the baltic energy market with the energy markets of scandinavia and central europe. the integration of the baltic region is uneven. trade and transport are developing rapidly in the region. the energy market is stagnating. the european commission has done some commendable work in this direction. the initiative to strengthen energy security and solidarity also includes the development of a baltic energy market interconnection plan. this will allow the baltic states to be gradually integrated into the single european energy market. i highly value sweden's involvement in the strategic discussions on the baltic sea region. sweden will have the opportunity to update it during the next six months of its european presidency. i am convinced that a strong european union is made up of strong regions from the mediterranean to the baltic. ladies and gentlemen! the european union's original objective - the safety and well-being of europe's citizens - has not changed. the environment in which we have to do this has changed. the world economy is much more interconnected than it was half a century ago. at the same time, new powerful economic players have emerged in the world. only by acting consistently, with foresight and, above all, in a united way, can the european union hope to remain in this global competition. only together can we deliver on the promises of security and prosperity to our citizens. only then can we achieve the goal for which the people of our countries have gone to the polls to support our membership of the european union. the european parliament has already shown in the past that it has a broad vision for the future of the european union. in particular, this applies to a fair and balanced approach to the union's enlargement policy. europe's dynamic growth process has enabled it to compete in the world. this growth is europe's potential and must be harnessed if the union is to continue to be an economic partner of equal value to the fast-growing economies of asia and latin america for decades to come. it is you, the democratically elected representatives of the european nations, who bear the greatest responsibility for this process. nor can the role of the european parliament in bringing the european project closer to the people and in increasing democratic legitimacy be overestimated. the role of the european parliament will be further strengthened. it's about uniting our diversity and our diversity. it is important to continue to work towards the completion of the european union. this is a task for all europeans to do together. this is our common responsibility towards europe. it is essential to avoid the fragmentation of the european union. member states must seek solutions and avoid the european project moving at different speeds. the agreement reached by the european council a month ago on the way forward for the lisbon treaty is welcome. the lisbon treaty is a legal prerequisite for the european union to continue to function fully and to strengthen its role on the international stage. only by putting the principles of the lisbon treaty into practice will we be able to realise the full positive potential of a new, united europe. the effectiveness of the lisbon treaty in practice depends on the political will and ability of member states and institutions to be united in achieving european objectives. ladies and gentlemen! until 2004, latvia's objective was to join the european union. since then, we have been framing latvia's goals in the context of european goals. we can no longer see ourselves and our world as separate from europe. latvia's objectives can only be defined and achieved if they are consistent with a common european vision for the future. european objectives, on the other hand, are achievable if they are consistent with the vision of each member state. the european union is built and must be strengthened on the basis of common values. only public debate can bring out the values we all share. only together can we agree on values that will go alongside those already laid down in the foundations of the european union. defining european values and stimulating debate on them is the task of all politicians, and in particular of european leaders. look to the future! how do i see the european union and latvia in the longer term? what about 2015? the post-crisis world economy will be a confluence of several european countries. in europe, countries will be judged on their achievements, not on geographical and geopolitical criteria. europe will be united by strong regions that, while defending their own interests, will work closely with others, thus creating a network of prosperity and development across europe. each country will contribute to development in accordance with its own capabilities and the president-in-office of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am speaking to you for the first time as president of the european council. the czech republic has taken over the leadership of the union from france, which i consider more than symbolic. france played a significant role in the birth of the modern czech state. the french court was the home of our greatest king, charles iv, emperor of the roman empire, who, after the example of the sorbonne in paris, founded the university of prague, one of the great institutions of european learning. we are therefore bound to france both for the fulfilment of our national aspirations and for the promotion of universal european values. just as it was not easy to establish a university in the czech republic that could be compared to the sorbonne, it is not easy to take over the presidency of the council of the eu after france. i see only one way to honor this task. it is no accident that i have chosen as an example of our connection with france and at the same time with european values a medieval monarch. charles iv could not defend the narrow czech positions in his politics and, on the contrary, had to integrate and represent the whole diverse empire. the european union is in a sense a continuation of medieval universalism. at least in that it puts a common moral code and a common legal basis above local power interests. there is talk of a second european union: bureaucratic, power-technological and spiritless. but i believe in the first europe, a europe of freedom, rights, ideas and rules. in this universe of values, where the law is elevated above the person, the size of the country doesn't matter. what matters is the ability to serve a common purpose. the role of the presidency is not to promote its interests or to make decisions. her role is to moderate and inspire debate. so i am not standing before you today as the prime minister of the czech republic, but as the president of the european council. the views i will be representing on this soil for the next six months will not be my own, nor will they be the views of the czech government. it will be a consensus of 27 countries embodied in the european council conclusions. i can't imagine being able to act any differently here. of course, as directly elected members of the european parliament, you have the right to ask me anything, and if you are interested, i will always be happy to give you my opinion or explain the czech position. but i don't think it's that important. the european council, which is also conceived the third millennium. a face that, in the spirit of the eu motto 'in varietate concordia', will be an expression of unity and diversity at the same time. as in the 19th century, the czechs are mantinels will enable us to play a more active role in breaking down external barriers, for example in international trade, and thus to better exploit the potential and comparative advantages of european countries. the czech republic will pursue these overarching objectives during the six months of its presidency, implementing three main programme areas, the three czech e: 1. economy, 2. energy and 3. the european union in the world. with a little exaggeration, it can be said that these 3 e's transformed into 2 g's at the beginning of the year gaz and gaza. if e is the energy in physics, then g is the symbol for gravitational acceleration. and 2g, that's a pretty decent overload for an untrained organism. i'm telling you, i could talk about priorities and tasks for hours. more than words, however, the results of the czech presidency so far are important. today is january 14th, which means we've been leading the eu for two weeks. in that time, we've managed to set up a political solution to the complicated russian gas problem and negotiate a deal between the two parties. we also led a european delegation to the middle east conflict area, which held a series of difficult negotiations with all actors and achieved initial successes in opening the humanitarian corridor to gaza. all this at a time when there was a critical situation at home around the reconstruction of the government and when we were exposed to attacks by the opposition, which irresponsibly torpedoes the czech presidency of the eu and takes the country's foreign commitments hostage in an internal political struggle. i think that the results we have achieved are more than a good answer to the doubting voices that the czech republic, for objective and subjective reasons, cannot manage the eu leadership. now, let's go into the areas in detail. first e: economics the czech presidency will focus on the proper implementation of the conclusions of the g20 summit declaration of november 2008 and the european council conclusions of december 2008. the key to success, according to these conclusions, is to avoid over-regulation and protectionism, i.e. to respect eu primary law, to respect the rules once they are in place. the eu must not close itself off from the world, but instead seek to make the world trade as open as possible and to make the most of it. at this point i would like to quote the words of my friend joseph daul of the epp_ed: 'the current economic crisis is not the defeat of capitalism but rather the result of political errors and the lack of rules for controlling financial markets.' the revision of the capital adequacy directive for investment firms and credit institutions, the negotiation of the insurance regulatory directive, the regulation on the activities of credit rating agencies and the directive on electronic money institutions will be priority agendas. the presidency will also seek to review the euro payments regulation and, last but not least, to ensure the timely and proper implementation of the economic and financial affairs council roadmaps adopted in response to the financial market crisis. at the same time, however, it is essential to analyse thoroughly the possibilities offered by the legislation currently in force and to make full use of them. only an economically strong and influential eu can address important issues of global politics, security, trade or the environment. the presidency must therefore devote itself to the implementation of the european economic recovery plan. we will emphasise its integration into the framework of the lisbon strategy: after short-term instruments to strengthen the economy, it will be time for instruments for medium and long-term structural reforms. the common agricultural policy is an example of this important structural reform. the key is to establish a level playing field for all eu member states in the payment of direct payments, both in terms of the amount of payments and the system for their payment (removal of historical disparities, taking into account the diversity of agriculture in each member state). we want to take this dimension into account in the debate on the future of the cap after 2013. in the long term, strengthening the eu's competitiveness is the best protection against the crushing effects of future crises. as i have already mentioned, this is about fully upholding and applying the four fundamental freedoms on which the union is founded. i would add the fifth freedom, the free movement of knowledge, which is a return to that medieval universalism. an important factor for improving competitiveness is the improvement of the quality of regulation, including the reduction of regulatory burdens, facilitating business, especially for smes. we're profiling this area a lot. in the area of foreign trade, the presidency will focus on reviving the wto debate. here we attach great importance to the successful completion of the doha development agenda (dda). the dda represents an effort to achieve transparent trade liberalisation at the multilateral level with long-term benefits. if the dda negotiations were to be interrupted, the presidency will seek to initiate reflection on multilateral trade instruments and will encourage greater intensity of negotiations on other wto agendas. and we must not forget about investing in education, research, development and innovation, improving the regulatory environment and reducing the administrative burden. and here i will quote the chairman of the social democratic group, martin schulz: 'europe cannot compete successfully with other regions of the world because of low wages and social standards, but because of technological innovation, higher quality of work, and the competence and knowledge of people.' i fully subscribe to that idea. second e: energy the second priority, like the first, is in the context of current developments. i'd just say more urgent and stronger. the global crisis may weaken europe in the short term. but the impending energy shortage would destroy not only europe's economy, but also our freedom and security, both immediately and in the long term. the czech presidency will continue its efforts to ensure a secure, competitive and sustainable energy for europe. in the field of energy security, we would like to focus on three dimensions of this issue: firstly, the completion of the second strategic energy review, which includes an analysis of the medium-term energy demand and supply in the eu and, on this basis, the identification of appropriate infrastructure projects. secondly, to complete the directive on the maintenance of minimum stocks of oil and petroleum products, where we support the increase of the mandatory minimum stocks from 90 to 120 days, and thirdly, to review the trans-european energy networks (tens-e), where the green paper on european energy networks is also part of the energy security legislation package adopted by the ec in november 2008. the reinforcement of infrastructure in the territory of the member states, including existing cross-border interconnections and the implementation of new interconnections of energy networks, is equally important. we hope for the support of the european parliament in all related legislative acts. naturally, we will also seek to diversify supply and transport routes. it is clear that, for example, the nabucco pipeline is a top priority, as is support for new pipelines. we must also seek to diversify the energy mix, including nuclear rehabilitation and investment in new technologies. the agreement we brokered to establish a monitoring mechanism for the transit of russian gas is a demonstration of the ability to achieve energy security in practice. the aim was to restore basic trust between the russian federation and ukraine and to bring elementary transparency to this issue. we've managed to get both countries to sign off on a single text, which could allow for deliveries to the european union. the eu must now take decisions and measures to avoid a repeat of the crisis with repercussions for member countries in the future. there is a need to increase transparency in the gas business, there is a need to diversify supply routes and suppliers. the eu's energy mix needs to be diversified. the development of safe nuclear energy needs to be seriously considered. infrastructure needs to be built up within the eu as a matter of urgency to connect member states efficiently, which is a prerequisite for an efficient gas market. in the area of the internal market and infrastructure, it is necessary to pursue effective coordination between transmission system operators, to complete the internal market in electricity and gas and to ensure the completion of the missing parts of the transmission and transport infrastructure. as regards the legislative priorities in this area, we want to conclude the third package for the internal energy market, i.e. to complete the revision of the two directives and the two regulations on electricity and gas, which aim to complete the liberalisation of the electricity and gas markets. we also aim to implement the regulation and establish an agency for regulatory cooperation. another area is energy efficiency, which the swedish presidency intends to tackle in greater depth, thus making the trio of france, the czech republic and sweden tackle the energy issue in a truly comprehensive and all-round way. although this priority is called energy, it is inextricably linked to climate policy. in this area, the presidency will seek to reach a globally acceptable agreement on the post-2012 reduction commitments, i.e. primarily to bring the us, india, china on board and pave the way for a broad international consensus at the end of 2009 in copenhagen. it should also reflect the current developments in the world economy. in the context of the coming economic recession and supply crisis, it will be particularly important to align environmental, competitiveness and safety requirements. the beginning of the year reminded us that the eu's priorities in the world have to deal with unforeseen pressing challenges. the new escalation of tensions between israel and hamas requires not only an active approach by the eu itself, but also coordination with major global and regional players. it is a further confirmation that peace cannot be achieved unless palestine begins to function as a fully-fledged state, capable of guaranteeing law and order and security to its neighbours in its territory. in addition to current diplomatic activities, the european union must therefore continue its efforts to build palestinian infrastructure, train security forces and strengthen the authority of the palestinian authority. the czech presidency will seek to use its good relations with both the palestinians and israel to resolve the conflict. but it is clear that without mutual trust, there can be no lasting peace in the middle east. i have already mentioned the eastern partnership here. the georgian crisis has shown how important it is for the eu to have a strategy in this area. the deepening of the eastern dimension of the european neighbourhood policy by strengthening cooperation with the countries of the region (primarily ukraine), as well as with the countries of the caucasus and caspian regions, is of great importance not only morally but also practically. this cooperation will allow us to diversify our foreign trade and supply of energy resources. as regards transatlantic relations, it is clear that without strengthening and developing them, the eu cannot effectively play its role as a strong global player, any more than the united states can play its role alone today. we can only succeed together in the long run. the czech presidency will therefore place emphasis on intensive dialogue with the new us administration in key areas of the economy, climate and energy, as well as cooperation with third countries (pakistan, afghanistan, russia, middle east). the position of the member states in the negotiations on the new partnership agreement with russia will also be crucial to the eu's standing in the world. the events of recent years and especially of recent months raise a number of questions and underline the need for a unified eu approach. it is based on an understanding of russia and a common analysis, which is why we will encourage cooperation between russia experts across the european union. the czech presidency will also continue negotiations on enlargement to include the western balkan countries and turkey. the western balkans must not be dragged into our economic problems and the current international crises. in the case of croatia, the presidency will do everything in its power to ensure that the union is enlarged as soon as possible. the positive example of croatia is a necessary precondition for maintaining the european perspective of other western balkan countries. we will certainly do our utmost to advance them through the stabilisation and association process. the czech presidency is also ready to continue developing the southern dimension of the european neighbourhood policy and improving relations with partner countries in the framework of this project. these include the strengthening of eu-israel relations and the middle east peace process in general, and the current dramatic developments in this area should not deter us. on the contrary, they emphasize the need to pursue a peaceful solution. the european priority in the world is, last but not least, the area of internal security. the nature of the current security threats is increasingly out of its reach. building an area of freedom, security and justice is a common eu interest that touches the lives of all our citizens. in this context, the presidency will seek to further progress in schengen cooperation, police and customs cooperation and cooperation between member states in civil and criminal matters. we are aware that the end of our presidency will be marked by the elections to the european parliament, a more tense political atmosphere and the need to delay the legislative process for selected legislative acts so that they do not fall under the table. we are also about to start discussions on a new european commission. he will also continue the debate with ireland on the fate of the lisbon treaty during the czech presidency. i believe that these talks must be conducted with sensitivity and with respect for the sovereignty of the irish people. moreover, if a referendum on the lisbon treaty were held in the czech republic, it would also not have passed. we must find a solution that the irish people can accept. which will no doubt help us in our domestic policy debate. i said at the beginning that the czech question is also a european question. perhaps no other nation has devoted as much space, effort and time to the debate about its own identity as the czechs. we know well from our own history what the european union is going through, as it searches for its own identity and the meaning of its existence. as the presidency, we therefore offer the community a two-decade experience of finding our own historical role, our own place in the family of european nations. the czech republic's relationship with europe was well-defined by the critic and philosopher františek václav krejčí more than seventy years ago: 'we do not mean the heart of europe in the czech republic in the geographical sense, but in the cultural and intellectual sense. we are in the very heart of the continent, where the influences of all its sides converge, and we feel surrounded by all the peoples of europe, if not directly, then at least thanks to the imaginative power of cultural creations. we call ourselves the crossroads of the currents of the mind, and that is why we are called to mediate, especially to mediate between the west and the east. i think these words are also inspiring at the beginning of 2009, when the czech republic has the task of moderating the debate in the european union for six months. thank you for your attention.
